dates.note: The HES record prints 'David Bryce 1864-70'; the node's exemplar prints 'Built 1863-69' with a year of 1869; the school's own history page and the Wikipedia article both give an opening in 1870. note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. The record is SHORT -- HES's own preamble says 'Earlier records may be brief and some information will not have been recorded' -- and it was extracted twice with the same result, so nothing here is being withheld for want of a second pass. THE ONE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST CONTRADICTS THE NODE'S HARD CONSTRAINT. HES classifies the building as 'Franco-Scottish gothic'; scottish-baronial.c03 forbids pointed arches, tracery and English bargeboards at hard severity, and the record then calls the chapel 'flamboyant', which is a Gothic tracery term. The node's exemplar note already reads Fettes as 'a Loire chateau crossed with the Scots tower house'; the register puts the emphasis further from Scotland than that. The main front is also 'symmetrical', against the node's declared picturesque-asymmetrical symmetry.
